key_insight: LTX-2 is an open-source, joint audio–visual foundation model that generates high-quality, temporally synchronized audiovisual content by modeling video and audio with an asymmetric dual-stream transformer.
problem_solved: Text-to-video generative models produce compelling visuals but lack aligned, semantically rich audio; LTX-2 addresses the missing audio modality and audiovisual synchronization in a unified model.
method: Asymmetric dual-stream transformer architecture: a 14B-parameter video stream paired with a 5B-parameter audio stream.
Bidirectional coupling between streams to enable cross-modal information flow and temporal synchronization of audio and video.
Unified generation pipeline that produces temporally aligned audiovisual outputs from shared/paired conditioning (e.g., text prompts).
impact: Provides practitioners with an efficient, open foundation for creating synchronized audio–visual content, enabling richer generative media, improved multimodal research, and practical downstream applications (e.g., film VFX, accessibility, multimedia synthesis).
visual_elements: Architecture diagram showing two parallel transformer streams (14B video, 5B audio) with bidirectional arrows indicating coupling.
Timeline visualization aligning video frames with audio waveform to illustrate temporal synchronization.
Parameter-size bar chart comparing video vs audio stream sizes and total model scale.
Example frame sequence + overlaid waveform or spectrogram to demonstrate joint audiovisual output.
paper_title: LTX-2: Efficient Joint Audio-Visual Foundation Model
paper_authors: Yoav HaCohen, Benny Brazowski, Nisan Chiprut, Yaki Bitterman, Andrew Kvochko
